newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb explodes in Russian region near Chechnya. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes in Russian region near Chechnya. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]

text.p: A bomb exploded near Russia's breakaway Chechnya region on Monday, the first anniversary of the death of separatist leader Dzhokhar Dudayev, but no casualties were reported, local officials said.

The bomb went off in the early hours in the city of Nalchik, in the southern Russian region of Kabardino-Balkaria about 70 km (45 miles) from the Chechnya border, regional prosecutor Ruslan Abazov told Reuters.
He told a Reuters cameraman in nearby Gekhi-Chu that a monument had suffered light damage.
(Corrects location of explosion from Gekhi-Chu to Nalchik)

A Moscow spokesman for the Federal Security Service said security had been stepped up around Chechnya, which is still seeking full independence from Moscow after a 21-month war which ended last August.

Abu Movsayev, leader of Chechnya's national security service, said last week some rebels could mark Dudayev's death by launching attacks in the neighbouring Russian regions of Kabardino-Balkaria, North Ossetia and Dagestan.
He said any attacks would not involve the Chechen leadership.

Dudayev declared Chechnya independent in 1991. He led the region's fight against Russian troops, sent to try to end the separatist drive in late 1994, until he was killed in a Russian rocket attack on April 21 last year.
